title: Generalized Lattice Model
body_html:
Generalized Lattice Model

Let \(W\) be a symplectic \(F\)-space and let \(B\) be a self-dual lattice function in \(W\). Put \(L=B_0\) and let \[ \ell_L=L/L^{\perp_\psi} \] be the finite symplectic quotient from Symplectic Annihilator Finite Quotient. The finite Heisenberg group attached to \(\ell_L\) has a unique irreducible representation with the chosen nontrivial central character, and the finite symplectic group acts on it through the finite Weil representation.

The generalized lattice model \(S(B_0)\) of the oscillator representation consists of locally constant compactly supported functions \[ f:W\to S(\ell_L) \] with the covariance rule \[ f(a+w)=\psi((1/2)\langle w,a\rangle_W)\,\omega_{\ell_L}(a)f(w), \qquad a\in B_0. \] This model gives a splitting of the metaplectic cover over the stabilizer of \(B_0\). Its restriction to the pro-unipotent subgroup is canonical.

For a dual pair and building points \(x\in B(G)\), \(x'\in B(G')\), the tensor-product lattice function \(B_{x,x'}\) supplies the lattice \(B_0\) used to compare \(K\)-types on both sides of theta correspondence.
